commit.subject: [ir] Require integral user-defined IO to have @interpolate(flat)
commit.message:
[ir] Require integral user-defined IO to have @interpolate(flat)

We recently added a check that @interpolate attributes on user-defined
IO always be `flat`, but we also need to check that the @interpolate
attribute is there at all for vertex outputs and fragment inputs.

Fixes a fuzzer test case.

Fixed: 474401152
Change-Id: Ib90418f18b3b6ecdbf41d422053fd851aff93012

commit.subject: Add tests for SetImmediates in RenderBundle
commit.message:
Add tests for SetImmediates in RenderBundle

This CL enables testing for SetImmediates command in RenderBundles by:
1. Adding end-to-end tests to verify SetImmediates execution and state persistence across bundles.
2. Refactoring validation tests (ImmediateDataTests.cpp) to properly parameterize over EncoderType.
3. Adding missing validation checks for SetImmediates in RenderBundles.

Bug: 366291600
Change-Id: I4cdf130bb20a56087b2a91d193b823be23770e10

commit.subject: Vulkan: Use CreateRenderPass2KHR when available.
commit.message:
Vulkan: Use CreateRenderPass2KHR when available.

Updates the Vulkan RenderPassCache to use CreateRenderPass2KHR when the
extension is available. This is required to use some dependent
extensions (like VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_single_sampled) if
dynamic rendering isn't available.

Attempts to unify the initialization code for VkRenderPassCreateInfo and
VkRenderPassCreateInfo2 as much as possible to avoid either duplicating
code or copying from one set of structs to the other.

Bug: 463893793
Change-Id: Ib06c88f2f22f871a4e4805d5f4df15f77db168bb

commit.subject: Remove auto lock from CreateTexture API calls
commit.message:
Remove auto lock from CreateTexture API calls

Add "no autolock" to Device::CreateTexture in dawn.json to prevent
automatic locking at the API boundary.

Introduce virtual method UseGuardForTextureCreationImpl() that
returns std::optional<DeviceGuard>. The default implementation
returns a guard, but D3D11 overrides to return nullopt since its
CreateTextureImpl is already thread-safe.

Lock acquisition must happen at the API level, not within Impl
methods, to avoid potential lock inversion issues when Impl methods
are called by other internal functions.

Bug: 474265307
Change-Id: I1f3df3e525c447abceeea9ec56e59791e071835f

Add "no autolock" to Device::CreateTexture in dawn.json to prevent
automatic locking at the API boundary.

Introduce virtual method UseGuardForTextureCreationImpl() that
returns std::optional<DeviceGuard>. The default implementation
returns a guard, but D3D11 overrides to return nullopt since its
CreateTextureImpl is already thread-safe.

Lock acquisition must happen at the API level, not within Impl
methods, to avoid potential lock inversion issues when Impl methods
are called by other internal functions.

This CL also does similar things for Device::CreateSampler.

Bug: 474265307
Change-Id: I1f3df3e525c447abceeea9ec56e59791e071835f

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Add ResourceTable mutator validation and state tracking
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Add ResourceTable mutator validation and state tracking

 - Update dawn.json to add ResourceTable::Update/Insert/RemoveBinding.
   The BindGroupEntryContents is changed to be a typedef to a
   BindingResource that's used by ResourceTable, this way
   DynamicArrayState doesn't need to change. (and bindless bindgroups
   will be removed soon).
 - Add a stub implementation of ResourceTable mutators in the wire.
 - Port all relevant tests from DynamicArrayValidationTests to
   ResourceTableValidationTests.

Bugs found with tests

 - Error resource tables didn't initialize the DynamicArrayState needed
   to do the state tracking.
 - ResourceTable::APIDestroy called Destroy which would skip calling
   DestroyImpl() on error objects.

Bug: 463925499
Change-Id: I20986c786dbb76665dd4d3c617972010a3fe5b26

commit.subject: Remove mInSubmit re-entrancy guard from ExecutionQueueBase
commit.message:
Remove mInSubmit re-entrancy guard from ExecutionQueueBase

The mInSubmit flag was added to prevent re-entrant calls to
SubmitPendingCommands() that could occur when DynamicUploader
automatically flushed pending commands after exceeding memory
thresholds.

After https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/263636, the
DynamicUploader no longer automatically flushes pending commands.

During Queue::Submit() itself, DynamicUploader operations only call
OnStagingMemoryFreePendingOnSubmit() to track memory usage without
triggering submissions. When memory thresholds are exceeded, the
submission is only triggered explicitly by subsequent calls to
MaybeSubmitPendingCommands() from API entry points. This makes
re-entrancy impossible, so the guard is no longer necessary.

Bug: 474265307
Change-Id: Ide2b98dc0d30b9ca91ccaf91d65c1d83383dd955

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Removes EventManager.Shutdown.

- Since Instance is no longer externally ref counted, we no longer
  need the EventManager.Shutdown to eagerly clean up callbacks
  that would otherwise leak. This also removes the need for the
  EventMap in the EventManager to be an optional.

commit.subject: [tint][val] Reject non-pipeline creatable values in RootBlock
commit.message:
[tint][val] Reject non-pipeline creatable values in RootBlock

This adds in a check to instructions in the root block validation to
ensure that they are either constants/overrides, or derived from them.

There is still some looseness to this check for expressions/builtins,
since it only checks that the operands, not if the expression/builtin
itself is allowed.

Fixes: 376624999

Change-Id: I95edd677df16180a2f23932a948d8f9fe0e74d44

commit.subject: Sync chromium-luci revision when rolling
commit.message:
Sync chromium-luci revision when rolling

Updates scripts/roll_chromium_deps.py to also sync the chromium-luci
revision in //infra/config/global/PACKAGE.star. This helps prevent
the shared Starlark code from getting out of date.

The associated change to the chromium-dawn autoroller to run
"lucicfg generate infra/config/global/main.star" needs to land first,
otherwise this could cause the roller to fail due to files generated
from Starlark being out of date.

Also drive-by fixes a few minor issues that were found elsewhere in the
script while working on it.

Bug: 452840620
Change-Id: Ida3261ad31cd501b889d4ba6760c71684ad03ba7

commit.subject: Fix ApiObjectBase::IsAlive() not thread-safe
commit.message:
Fix ApiObjectBase::IsAlive() not thread-safe

ApiObjectBase::IsAlive() is not thread safe because it checks
LinkedNode's next pointer which could be modified by its neighbor nodes'
RemoveFromList() calls.

Fix by using relaxed atomic pointers in LinkedNode.

commit.subject: [dawn][fuzz] Fix the fuzzers to use spontaneous callbacks.
commit.message:
[dawn][fuzz] Fix the fuzzers to use spontaneous callbacks.

- Recent changes to remove external references for Instances
  exposed a bug in the fuzzers where it was relying on dropping
  the last external reference to the instance to clean up
  outstanding callbacks.
- By making the fuzzer server use spontaneous callbacks like
  what we do in production, this allows the callbacks to run
  and prevent leaking the callbacks.

Bug: 474854046
Change-Id: I0cb85a9158a5c67832a56e36c3d911c5bba6863f

commit.subject: [dawn] Move texture gather offset failures to permanent
commit.message:
[dawn] Move texture gather offset failures to permanent

Texture sampling with offsets is a known edge case for which there is
vulkan cts exceptions for specific devices.

I would not expect these to ever be fixed and I would assume these
are very low priority polyfills.

(a polyfill might be possible but one would need to sample the texture
dimensions etc)

commit.subject: Avoid device guard in WaitForQueueSerial()
commit.message:
Avoid device guard in WaitForQueueSerial()

Change ExecutionQueueBase::WaitForQueueSerial() to only acquire the
device mutex if waitSerial is newer than last submitted serial.
GetLastSubmittedCommandSerial() gets an atomic so mutex isn't need to
check it. This ensures WaitForQueueSerial() won't block on device mutex
unless it's actually needed.

Bug: 412761228
Change-Id: Ief1e54deff71f9f692f3e92c887a1d5b7ce070ae

commit.subject: [dawn] Make the Instance simply RefCounted.
commit.message:
[dawn] Make the Instance simply RefCounted.

- Before, the Instance needed to be externally refcounted because
  there wasn't a way to get the Instance once the last external
  reference was dropped, hence it could cause any WaitAnyOnly or
  AllowProcessEvent events to be leaked. Since then, we have
  added a `GetInstance()` API on the Adapter which means that as
  long as we have a Device (which has `GetAdapter()`) on it, the
  instance can be reached. As a result, we only need to clear all
  events when the last device reference is dropped. This means
  that the Instance can just be a simple refcounted object now.
- This is also necessary because the `WaitAny()` and
  `ProcessEvents()` APIs implicitly assume that if they are called,
  that the Instance is externally alive. However, because users
  can drop the last external reference, then get a new one when
  they need it via the Device/Adapter, some teardown code in
  Chromium could cause a crash by calling those APIs on an
  Instance retrieved via the getter APIs after the original
  external reference was dropped.

Bug: 467732049
Change-Id: Ib04c6243538983c2ba4c3060beb23487da66a499

commit.subject: Convert CMake builder to chromium-luci code
commit.message:
Convert CMake builder to chromium-luci code

Converts cmake-linux-clang-rel-x64 to use the shared chromium-luci
Starlark code used by the GN builders and updates its name to the
convention standardized on as part of the migration to the gn_v2
builders.

The new builders should be functionally equivalent to the old ones.

Bug: 459517292
Change-Id: I6d3246ae70bff82000b09a364fb654076a7f800c

commit.subject: Add CMake builder suing chromium-luci code
commit.message:
Add CMake builder suing chromium-luci code

Adds an equivalent to cmake-linux-clang-rel-x64 defined using the shared
chromium-luci Starlark code. The legacy builder is still kept for now,
as the new builder is CI-only with a manual trybot mirror. However, once
we confirm that the new builder works as expected, it will replace the
legacy one.

The new builders should be functionally equivalent to the old ones.

Bug: 459517292
Change-Id: I6d3246ae70bff82000b09a364fb654076a7f800c

commit.subject: [bindless][wire] Implement ResourceTable in the wire
commit.message:
[bindless][wire] Implement ResourceTable in the wire

 - Add client-side tracking for ResourceTable mutators using the Queue's
   last/completed submit indices.
 - Update/RemoveBinding have custom commands that don't return a
   wgpu::Status and instead the server checks that the client only sends
   commands that will resulst in successful Update/RemoveBinding calls
   on the server side.
 - Add support for ResourceTableLimits in the client and the server.
 - Move the logic to lazily create the queue on the client::Device to a
   new GetQueue getter that's used by the ResourceTable and APIGetQueue
   where lazy creation used to happen.
 - Enables all the ResourceTable on the wire.

Fixed: 473444513
Change-Id: Idc0b50d84a8e47851558f1a4f5fcfaebcf56d9e4

commit.subject: [dawn][wire] Support generating server doers for wgpu::Status returns
commit.message:
[dawn][wire] Support generating server doers for wgpu::Status returns

When a WebGPU command returns a wgpu::Status, it is used to
synchronously say if a validation error happened. On the server side,
check that the client always sends valid commands by checking that the
WGPUStatus is Success.

The only such method (that's not client side for other reasons )is
Surface::Present but a follow-up CL will also add ResourceTable::Update
and RemoveBinding.

Bug: 473444513
Change-Id: I4f7aa26dadb6068b0633fe7941d38e19b82e15e3

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Implement validation for immediate data
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Implement validation for immediate data

This CL implements validation for immediate data usage in Dawn.
It adds VALIDATION_ASPECT_IMMEDIATE_DATA to CommandBufferStateTracker
to track if the required immediate data has been set before dispatch
or draw.

It also updates Pipeline::Initialize to validate that the shader does
not use immediate constants outside the range defined in the
PipelineLayout.

ShaderModule is updated to populate immediateDataUsedSlots in the
entry point metadata, which is used by the pipeline validation.

Unit tests in ImmediateDataTests.cpp are refactored and expanded to
cover these validation cases.

Bug: 366291600
Change-Id: Iaeb606152439d92c6d535466b5e171300ec4eee8

commit.subject: Add `TINT_CHECK_RESULT_ASSIGN` macro.
commit.message:
Add `TINT_CHECK_RESULT_ASSIGN` macro.

This CL extends the idea from adding `TINT_CHECK_RESULT` to an
assignment version, so instead of doing:

```
auto val = SomeCalculation();
TINT_CHECK_RESULT(val);
```

This CL allows:

```
TINT_CHECK_RESULT_ASSIGN(val, SomeCalculation());
```

This solves the issue where you have a series of assignments and checks
and you accidentally pass in the wrong result to validate.

The `_ASSIGN` will assign the type as the value inside the Result. This
removes the need to call `.Get()` or `.Move()` on the result as it's
been done automatically.

Bug: 474126156
Change-Id: I752c4351d0bcf128e6ac1c37dd0ee2b14a1ab147

commit.subject: Capture: Only copy Align(size,4) of buffers.
commit.message:
Capture: Only copy Align(size,4) of buffers.

Buffers are allowed to be any size but copyBufferToBuffer requires
4 byte alignment for both size and offset which prevents us from
copying the trailing bytes. writeBuffer has the same alignment
requirements. so the user can't put bytes in via writeBuffer.
mapAsync requires offset to be 8 byte aligned and size to be 4
bytes so the user can not set those last bytes with mapAsync. We
can still access those bytes with copyBufferToTexture and
copyTextureToBuffer though. 

For now, we just ignore the last 3 bytes. This fixes
BufferZeroInitTest.PaddingInitialized/WebGPU_WebGPU_backend_on_BackendType__Metal_Apple_M1_Max__e_nonzero_clear_resources_on_creation_for_testing

Bug: 473593119
Change-Id: I6a6a6964e9c12f0cbe353840940547f36dbb3e9c

commit.subject: Capture: Only copy Align(size,4) of buffers.
commit.message:
Capture: Only copy Align(size,4) of buffers.

Buffers are allowed to be any size but copyBufferToBuffer requires
4 byte alignment for both size and offset which prevents us from
copying the trailing bytes. writeBuffer has the same alignment
requirements. so the user can't put bytes in via writeBuffer.
mapAsync requires offset to be 8 byte aligned and size to be 4
bytes so the user can not set those last bytes with mapAsync. We
can still access those bytes with copyBufferToTexture and
copyTextureToBuffer though. 

For now, we just ignore the last 3 bytes. This fixes
BufferZeroInitTest.PaddingInitialized/WebGPU_WebGPU_backend_on_BackendType__Metal_Apple_M1_Max__e_nonzero_clear_resources_on_creation_for_testing

Bug: 473593119

commit.subject: Change tint emission for multiple entry points.
commit.message:
Change tint emission for multiple entry points.

Currently, if you provide an output file like `-o foo.hlsl` and the
given `wgsl` we change the name of the output file to inject the entry
point name (so you may get `foo.main.hlsl` output instead).

This behaviour is confusing, instead, if `-o` is provided but `--ep` is
not and there are multiple entry points, we emit an error and require an
entry point to be provided.

This does not effect emitting to stdout, you'll still get all of the
entry points emitted. It also does not require `--ep` if there is only a
single entry point in the WGSL file.

Bug: 473791193
Change-Id: I849b722e83bd35b44a4cc56f53e59a68ed2fa213

commit.subject: LazyClearRenderPass shoud be skipped if lazy clear toggle is off
commit.message:
LazyClearRenderPass shoud be skipped if lazy clear toggle is off

Currently LazyClearRenderPass is still called even when
LazyClearResourceOnFirstUse toggle is off. This could lead to
correctness issues when this toggle is disabled by users. For example:
1. A texture A is created.
2. A buffer is copied to the upper half of the texture A.
  - Lazy clear is disabled here.
3. Texture A's lower half is rendered in a render pass.
  - Before the render pass is started, LazyClearRenderPass would be
    triggered and clear the entire texture, erase its upper half.

This CL fixes it by skipping LazyClearRenderPass when the toggle is
disabled.

Bug: chromium:474289075
Change-Id: I1488503794b8e15db16357f3f8764b4e2d319d36

commit.subject: Add optional memory dump owner GUID for texture
commit.message:
Add optional memory dump owner GUID for texture

This CL add a optional DawnMemoryDumpOwnershipDescriptor chained in
TextureDescriptor to provide a owner GUID that recorded in TextureBase
when creating Texture and get reported during memory dumping. This can
help us better understand the texture memory usage for shared images in
Chromium.

Issue: 397989391
Change-Id: I5cfca178b9474ac62ec6d783dd879530eec63d38

commit.message:
Improve new webgpu test ID handling for CTS Roller

The CTS roller was producing malformed expectation lines due to a recent
change in the test ID format. This change adapts the new test IDs to
the legacy format expected by the roller.

A new test case has been added to verify these transformations and
prevent future regressions.

Bug:473575364
Change-Id: I8f69aed0677b0e19330227f6a0fb6bbaa1b667fd

commit.subject: [ir] Check for duplicate offset in AddInternalImmediateData
commit.message:
[ir] Check for duplicate offset in AddInternalImmediateData

Returning a failure allows the backends to propagate this back to the
caller gracefully instead of crashing inside later transforms.

Fixes a fuzzer bug that had duplicate internal immediate offsets.

Fixed: 470193768
Change-Id: I6187d5a48f5872d548c636f4d138a957380232d7

commit.subject: Revert "[dawn][d3d] Adds loop for WaitForMultipleObjects with INFINITY."
commit.message:
Revert "[dawn][d3d] Adds loop for WaitForMultipleObjects with INFINITY."

This reverts commit 2bf640bbd9f73e703855650d02f844e7e485a927.

Reason for revert: Suppression removals were premature.

Original change's description:
> [dawn][d3d] Adds loop for WaitForMultipleObjects with INFINITY.
>
> - Adding the loop addresses the reverted workaround.
> - Also includes a small fix for potential race in spontaneous
>   event handling.
> - Re-enables all the related tests now that they seem to be
>   passing fine now on the arm64 Qualcomm devices with this fix.
> - Also reverts "Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free"
>   commit 37905ab50503cb442aac9a8a28ac7306416dee39.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free
> >
> > Fixes an issue where the callback registered in
> > DawnTestBase::MapAsyncAndWait could cause an access violation during
> > global test teardown due to trying to run a callback that was allocated
> > on the stack and had already gone out of scope. This only occurred when
> > instance.WaitAny() timed out, which would cause the callback to still
> > be around until the instance got destroyed and ensured that all pending
> > callbacks were complete.
> >
> > Now, the actual callback to run is provided via a shared_ptr and the
> > lambda provided to buffer.MapAsync() checks if it is null before running
> > it. After instance.WaitAny() returns but before we make any asserts, we
> > set the pointer to null, preventing the soon-to-be-dangling pointer from
> > being used in the future.
> >
> > This is meant as a temporary workaround, as WaitAny() should always run
> > the provided callback. This can be reverted once the underlying issue
> > is fixed.
> >
> > Bug: 459864803, 460743383
> > Change-Id: I5384e74ff6ab9da6104b07e6d9d235bf5d4b40c2
> > Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/273736
> > Commit-Queue: Brian Sheedy <bsheedy@google.com>
> > Reviewed-by: Loko Kung <lokokung@google.com>
> > Auto-Submit: Brian Sheedy <bsheedy@google.com>

>

commit.subject: Statically request Vulkan API version 1.1
commit.message:
Statically request Vulkan API version 1.1

Changes Vulkan instance creation to always request Vulkan 1.1 rather
than the highest available API version. Previously Dawn required at
least 1.1, so no devices are excluded by this change.

Any extensions that were promoted to core in 1.1 have corresponding
checks and fallback code paths removed. Function pointers for 1.1 are
always queried, and for extensions not in 1.1 postfixed versions of the
function name are always used. Logic to omit extension strings during
device creation is removed since it was being improperly applied and
could result in being unable to query function pointers for promoted
extensions.

Bug: 469279054
Change-Id: I044fccee8af55ba876bb8e0499e1e7c78a8840ad

commit.subject: Revert "Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free"
commit.message:
Revert "Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free"

This reverts commit 37905ab50503cb442aac9a8a28ac7306416dee39.

Reason for revert: Fixes the root cause of the workaround.

Original change's description:
> Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free
>
> Fixes an issue where the callback registered in
> DawnTestBase::MapAsyncAndWait could cause an access violation during
> global test teardown due to trying to run a callback that was allocated
> on the stack and had already gone out of scope. This only occurred when
> instance.WaitAny() timed out, which would cause the callback to still
> be around until the instance got destroyed and ensured that all pending
> callbacks were complete.
>
> Now, the actual callback to run is provided via a shared_ptr and the
> lambda provided to buffer.MapAsync() checks if it is null before running
> it. After instance.WaitAny() returns but before we make any asserts, we
> set the pointer to null, preventing the soon-to-be-dangling pointer from
> being used in the future.
>
> This is meant as a temporary workaround, as WaitAny() should always run
> the provided callback. This can be reverted once the underlying issue
> is fixed.
>
> Bug: 459864803, 460743383
> Change-Id: I5384e74ff6ab9da6104b07e6d9d235bf5d4b40c2
> Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/273736

> on the stack and had already gone out of scope. This only occurred when

> be around until the instance got destroyed and ensured that all pending
> callbacks were complete.

> lambda provided to buffer.MapAsync() checks if it is null before running
> it. After instance.WaitAny() returns but before we make any asserts, we

> being used in the future.

> This is meant as a temporary workaround, as WaitAny() should always run
> the provided callback. This can be reverted once the underlying issue

commit.subject: [dawn] Support surrogates when converting UTF8 offsets to UTF16
commit.message:
[dawn] Support surrogates when converting UTF8 offsets to UTF16

While surrogates are technically invalid code points in UTF-16, most
software supports it and Tint doesn't validate them out during parsing.
For that reason, this CL adds support for surrogates in
CountUTF16CodeUnitsFromUTF8String, which removes the need for error
handing in CompilationMessages::AddMessages().

Update hte CountUTF16CodeUnitsFromUTF8String tests to check surrogates
are supported and remove the error tests from it. Instead replace them
with tests that compilation errors are produced when creating a shader
with invalid UTF8.

Fixed: 471714206
Change-Id: I8b4cd59b766b5e7e06cd3e59052900dbf2fa5819

commit.subject: [tint] Add --update-skip E2E test runner option
commit.message:
[tint] Add --update-skip E2E test runner option

The `--generate-skip` option is usually used to generate skip files
for newly added tests. It currently also updates all existing skip
files, which makes CLs very noisy.

This CL changes the behavior to only generate new skip files, and adds
a new `--update-skip` option that can be used to regenerate existing
skip files instead.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] add a DestroyReason argument to DestroyImpl.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] add a DestroyReason argument to DestroyImpl.

This will be useful to determine what caused DestroyImpl to be called
because sometimes the behavior needs to change based on whether
DestroyImpl is called from inside DeleteThis (no extra ref to the object
must be taken), or from another Destroy reason (like the API Destroy
call, device loss, etc).

The vast majority of the changes were done with the following commands:

```
git grep -l "::DestroyImpl();" | xargs sed -i "" "s/::DestroyImpl();/::DestroyImpl(reason);/"
git grep -l "DestroyImpl() {" | xargs sed -i "" "s/DestroyImpl() {/DestroyImpl(DestroyReason reason) {/"
git grep -l "DestroyImpl() override" | xargs sed -i "" "s/DestroyImpl() override/DestroyImpl(DestroyReason reason) override/"
git grep -l "void, DestroyImpl, ()," | xargs sed -i "" "s/void, DestroyImpl, (),/void, DestroyImpl, (DestroyReason),/"
git grep -l "DestroyImpl).WillByDefault(\[this\] {" | xargs sed -i "" "s/DestroyImpl).WillByDefault(\[this\] {/DestroyImpl).WillByDefault(\[this\](DestroyReason reason) {/"
git cl format
```

commit.subject: [bindless][wire] Track queue last and completed submits
commit.message:
[bindless][wire] Track queue last and completed submits

The content-timeline validation of ResourceTable requires knowing when
queue submits are completed (which is when slots can be reused). Add
a call to OnSubmittedWorkDone right after sending the QueueSubmitCmd in
dawn::wire::client::Queue for that purpose.

Also adds a wire test that the queue's OnSubmittedWorkDone happens
before any user OnSubmittedWorkDone.

Change-Id: I0db7fda23f48b79e14760c046d1783621992bbba

commit.subject: [tint] Support attribute `@subgroup_size` on HLSL backend
commit.message:
[tint] Support attribute `@subgroup_size` on HLSL backend

This patch supports the translation from attribute `@subgroup_size`
to `[WaveSize] on HLSL backend and disables the support of this
attribute on GLSL and MSL backend. On Vulkan `@subgroup_size` will
be set on the API side instead of the SPIR-V so we don't need to
handle `@subgroup_size` on the SPIR-V backend.

Bug: 463721943
Change-Id: I58fb55f35ba6bb7c771ef03556a11c63a8a4e50a

commit.subject: [github] Only run ci.yml as part of nightly releases
commit.message:
[github] Only run ci.yml as part of nightly releases

We don't really need to run this on every commit anymore now that it
runs nightly as part of the nightly release.

We also don't really need to run it on pull_request because it only runs
on GitHub PRs (not Gerrit CLs), and even so reviewers only pay attention
to the test results the mirrored-to-Gerrit CL.

Bug: 430624000
Change-Id: Id3f8a55df0bf3235a91f526279b1ff249302caf5

commit.subject: Add binary releases via github actions
commit.message:
Add binary releases via github actions

Fixes https://issues.chromium.org/issues/409590665. See also https://issues.chromium.org/issues/409590665#comment6.

Here's an example of how the release would look: https://github.com/jacksonrl/dawn/releases/tag/v20251223.163459-jacksonrl.dawn.main The only difference is the name wouldn't have my name in it, which I think is autogenerated due to being a fork, and it would contain the macos/ios builds as well, which I disabled in my local version when testing due to low balance for macos runners (diff: https://github.com/jacksonrl/dawn/compare/7d88c22000b7d6941a7603851ac68d9f930c1947...e53c2d023762254bb7b884a13d5e9dd10b14d214)

There are some ways we could improve the release outputs, but I wanted to make as minimal changes as possible to prevent any breakage as I cannot test all these platforms. Therefore this just uploads the output from the existing CI, which is mentioned in 409590665. These are nightly releases so nobody is expecting them to be stable, we can always improve this later

This also fixes the emdawnwebgpu release which was broken by https://github.com/google/dawn/commit/0979968b84312b7c52521739ef93eb9812f0f3ed by removing `wgpuTextureGetTextureBindingViewDimension` from the emdawnwebgpu header. I'm not too familiar with the codebase so someone should please check that that is valid.

Motivation: Many people end up needing graphics at some point. Having prebuilt binaries allows people to choose WebGPU more readily, which strengthens the WebGPU ecosystem (eg. more libraries made with wglsl) and also allows people to potentially port their code to web at a later point.

commit.subject: Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free
commit.message:
Fix MapAsyncAndWait use-after-free

Fixes an issue where the callback registered in
DawnTestBase::MapAsyncAndWait could cause an access violation during
global test teardown due to trying to run a callback that was allocated
on the stack and had already gone out of scope. This only occurred when
instance.WaitAny() timed out, which would cause the callback to still
be around until the instance got destroyed and ensured that all pending
callbacks were complete.

Now, the actual callback to run is provided via a shared_ptr and the
lambda provided to buffer.MapAsync() checks if it is null before running
it. After instance.WaitAny() returns but before we make any asserts, we
set the pointer to null, preventing the soon-to-be-dangling pointer from
being used in the future.

Bug: 459864803
Change-Id: I5384e74ff6ab9da6104b07e6d9d235bf5d4b40c2

Add idlgen run tests

Adds test coverage for //tools/src/cmd/idlgen's run function. More
specific tests for underlying helper functions will be added in
follow-up CLs.

Also fixes a found issue where there was code to support outputting to
stdout, but it was unreachable since the --output argument was treated
as required.

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Renames to use ResourceTable terminology
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Renames to use ResourceTable terminology

Clean up a few remaining uses of the "dynamic array" terminology to use
ResourceTable instead.

 - kReservedDynamicBindingArrayEntries -> kReservedResourceTableSlots
 - DynamicArrayDefaultBindings -> ResourceTableDefaultResources as well
   as related members and getters.
 - TextureBase::DynamicArraySlot -> ResourceTableSlotUse as well as
   related members and methods.

Also remove a TODO about a potential UAF that's no longer current and
replace it with a comment (in CommandEncoder.h).

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Simplify code after the removal of "dynamic binding array"
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Simplify code after the removal of "dynamic binding array"

 - Inline BindGroupLayoutStaticBindingOnly in BindGroupLayout since it
   is now the only child class.
 - Inline BindGroup::InitializeStaticBindings in Initialize since it is
   now the only code path.
 - Inline DescriptorSetAllocatorDynamicArray in ResourceTable and
   simplify the code.

commit.subject: Refactor idlgen for better testing
commit.message:
Refactor idlgen for better testing

Slightly refactors //tools/src/cmd/idlgen/main.go to better accommodate
future testing. Changes include:

* Making showUsage return an error instead of calling os.Exit
* Making run not rely on global flag state
* Updating parsing code to read and parse a file instead of relying on
  ParseFiles, as that circumvents the filesystem dependency injection

All of these changes should be functional no-ops outside of tests.

Bug: 344014313
Change-Id: I7c22c1437b337df1714adab0f9e50fc2ec828527

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Assert Pipeline Is Set Before Applying Immediates
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Assert Pipeline Is Set Before Applying Immediates

Replace early return with an assertion to ensure that the pipeline is set
before applying immediate constants in D3D11, D3D12, and Vulkan backends.

This change helps catch potential issues where immediate constants are
attempted to be applied without a valid pipeline.

[dawn][native] Assert Pipeline Is Set Before Applying Immediates

Replace early return with an assertion to ensure that the pipeline is
set before applying immediate constants in D3D11, D3D12, and Vulkan
backends.

This change helps catch potential issues where immediate constants are
attempted to be applied without a valid pipeline.

Bug: 366291600
Change-Id: Icf4f988909ac63933056b18031206f6201f9cc75

commit.subject: Explicitly list generator dependencies
commit.message:
Explicitly list generator dependencies

Updates dawn_json_generator and a template it depends on to properly
declare and handle dependencies on various JSON files used for
generation.

Previously, we solely relied on an underlying usage of a depfile
argument to surface these dependencies, which worked on the older GN
recipe that did not use `gn analyze` on trybots. However, since the
gn_v2 recipe automatically uses `gn analyze` to avoid unnecessary
compilations and depfile appears to be only usable at build time
(whereas `gn analyze` uses static analysis), not explicitly declaring
the dependency on the JSON files allows regressions caused by those
files to make it past the CQ.

Bug: 466134210
Change-Id: I921307d6ecb5dc6172d241a583ad0adfe7eaa472

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Disallow 0 texture usage even with internal usages
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Disallow 0 texture usage even with internal usages

Previously `usage` could be zero as long as `internalUsage` was nonzero.
But the spec requires `usage=0` to be a validation error. The extension
shouldn't change this.

This fixes a test I'm adding in https://github.com/gpuweb/cts/pull/4527

Bug: 468353736
Change-Id: Ibeb6d4b539701ee93d6039792e62d5a77aa2ca71

commit.subject: native: Handle BlobCache mLoadFunction size mismatch as cache miss
commit.message:
native: Handle BlobCache mLoadFunction size mismatch as cache miss

BlobCache currently calls mLoadFunction twice for a load request,
expecting identical sizes. This isn't guaranteed due to potential
external cache evictions or IO/timeout issues between calls. Instead of
crashing, this CL treats a size mismatch as a cache miss.

Future work should update mLoadFunction to return a memory buffer
directly, eliminating the two-call requirement.

Bug: chromium:469351711
Change-Id: If25c0e6a94ab0e00595a8deb5062f46ddfbea975

commit.message:
[inspector] Implement GetImmediateBlockInfo

This CL implements a helper function GetImmediateBlockInfo in the
inspector. It returns a Bitset<16> indicating which 4-byte slots
of the immediate block are accessible (used) by the entry point.
This handles padding in structs and matrices correctly.

commit.subject: [dawn] Remove ChromiumExperimentalBindless
commit.message:
[dawn] Remove ChromiumExperimentalBindless

It has been superseeded by ChromiumExperimentalResourceTable. This
change was done by removing all ChromiumExperimentalBindless changes to
dawn.json and deleting code paths until everything compiles again. Some
renames are done in this commit, but a bunch of TODOs for additional
cleanups are added as well, mostly to re-inline objects that were split
for dynamic binding array support.

Bug: 463925499
Change-Id: I1514fb8e7e15851d35eb3d03a3556a76cb7a0615

commit.subject: Run test spec presubmit on DEPS changes
commit.message:
Run test spec presubmit on DEPS changes

Refactors the existing presubmit to ensure that the generated JSON files
under //infra/specs are up to date and runs it on changes to DEPS. This
helps catch issues of //testing being updated through DEPS and the test
specs getting out of date due to a change in Swarming dimensions.

Since a gclient sync is necessary to pull in the updated //testing
contents, it is possible for a manual roll to be uploaded without this
check being hit locally. However, the Dawn presubmit bot should fail in
such cases.

Bug: 452840620
Change-Id: Iaadf3a53b58c8bbd6e8c4b402a1ec80dc01b8415

commit.subject: Suppress perf tests on Mac/Intel
commit.message:
Suppress perf tests on Mac/Intel

Suppresses UniformBufferUpdatePerf on Mac/Intel when running multiple
uniform buffers at full upload size. This combination of hardware and
parameters flakily results in a pure virtual function being called,
which then causes the entire task to fail.

This practically only occurs on the AMD Macbooks when using their
integrated GPUs, but there is currently no way to differentiate those
from the Mac Minis with Intel GPUs that are not running into this.

Bug: 468353718
Change-Id: If675cafc664ad2c5a727aae159b24cfd58f77f05

wip check-capture-replay flag

Add --check-capture-replay flag for dawn_end2end_tests.

Add a allowlist toggle enable_for_check_capture_replay at the
same time. Since many tests will fail checking capture_replay
at this time, instead of suppressing failure tests, we turn on
passing tests by specifying a
WebGPUBackend({"enable_for_check_capture_replay"}) config.

Locally we can run dawn_end2end_tests with --check-capture-replay
and --enable-toggles=enable_for_check_capture_replay at the same
time to turn on check capture replay.

Once implementation are more complete we can remove
enable_for_check_capture_replay.

Add check-capture-replay flag

Add --check-capture-replay flag for dawn_end2end_tests.
When it's on it turns on capture the test body. On Teardown
it finish capturing and replay the capture. It pauses capturing
for buffer expectation copy and for each of these readback buffer
it checks the content of the replayed one to see if it's expected.

for the replayed readback buffer slot and resolve together

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Skip DynamicArrayState resource updates for empty slots
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Skip DynamicArrayState resource updates for empty slots

This moves the logic to skip resource updates for empty slots in the
frontend since all backends will just keep leftover resources in now
unused slots, and assume that shader validation will prevent access.

Bug: 463925499
Change-Id: Id97667985eced82e699ac974956dfa459a1bf532

commit.subject: Disable DXGI's alt+enter fullscreen handling
commit.message:
Disable DXGI's alt+enter fullscreen handling

DXGI will listen for alt+enter and go fullscreen in response to this shortcut, sometimes in broken ways. Disable this behavior to allow applications to handle this shortcut using their own logic (if desired). Note that MakeWindowAssociation must be called after swapchain creation, and using the same DXGIFactory used to create the swapchain.

This is an imported pull request from
https://github.com/google/dawn/pull/53

commit.subject: [ir] Improve validation speed with many failures
commit.message:
[ir] Improve validation speed with many failures

ReserveAdditional() was being used to grow the diagnostics vector by
only two slots at a time, which was triggering many copies of the
diagnostics vector for modules that have many failures. Instead just
let the vector grow naturally (which doubles the size when needed) and
manully get the reference to the error diagnostic.

Also add an early exit when iterating over instructions and errors
have already been found.

Fixed: 466695523
Change-Id: I8b862c8550237d29c75fa9d1a1aa150cf4fc86fa

state of robustness. Remove the guard on setting the default to true.

commit.subject: [dawn][tests] Allow using ASSERT_DEVICE_ERROR in helper functions
commit.message:
[dawn][tests] Allow using ASSERT_DEVICE_ERROR in helper functions

In ValidationTest, ASSERT_DEVICE_ERROR used GTest's FAIL() macro with
immediately returns and prevents usage of it in helper functions that
return a value. Instead use ADD_FAILURE that doesn't cause an early
return.

Change-Id: I0311509e9c3a42ca97b9bfc45f3975880c33b31b

commit.message:
[dawn][native] Disallow GetBGL(3) with resource tables.

The resource tables use one bind group slot so it doesn't make sense to
query the BGL at position maxBindGroups - 1 since it conceptually
doesn't exist.

commit.subject: [ir] Validate attribute `subgroup_size` in IR validator
commit.message:
[ir] Validate attribute `subgroup_size` in IR validator

This patch adds the attribute `subgroup_size` and all the related
validation in Tint IR validator.
- `subgroup_size` must be a constant or override expression
- `subgroup_size` must be `i32` or `u32`.
- `subgroup_size` must be greater than 0.
- `subgroup_size` must be a power of 2.

Bug: 463721943
Change-Id: I9de573e6253de3f66d0ee4809674d5f49881671a

commit.subject: [ir] Fix validation order for control flow
commit.message:
[ir] Fix validation order for control flow

Make sure we validate blocks nested in control flow before we validate
instructions that follow the control flow instruction.

This fixes an issue where values declared after a control flow
instruction were incorrectly seen as in scope inside that control flow
instruction.

Fixed: 467610939
Change-Id: I43c88601ff041e084475f17d814858af193a72d5

if newState != BufferState::Destroyed.

Specify the existing Qualcomm WebGPU CTS expectations as Android

commit.subject: Remove autolock from Buffer::Unmap()
commit.message:
Remove autolock from Buffer::Unmap()

Don't lock the device mutex during buffer Unmap() where possible. A new
BufferState is added to signal the buffer is inside an operation. If
multiple threads try to change the state concurrently a validation error
is thrown.

The backend implementation may still need to lock the device mutex
during UnmapImpl() if it's not thread safe. For Vulkan and Metal that
isn't required so unmapping a buffer won't block.

Change-Id: I79f8314e8bcbf8a1eb5672cf28e72edb984e7643

commit.subject: Remove autolock from Buffer::Unmap()
commit.message:
Remove autolock from Buffer::Unmap()

Don't lock the device mutex when wgpu::Buffer::Unmap() is called. This
relies on access to buffers being externally synchronized by the dawn
client so buffer unmapping shouldn't overlap with other use of the
buffer.

To help guard against concurrent use a new BufferState is added to
signal the buffer is inside an operation. At the start of MapAsync() and
Unmap() the buffer state is exchanged. If multiple threads try to change
the state concurrently a validation error gets thrown.

The backend may still need to lock the device mutex during UnmapImpl()
if it's not thread safe. For Vulkan and Metal that isn't required so
unmapping a buffer won't block.

commit.subject: Remove autolock from Buffer operations
commit.message:
Remove autolock from Buffer operations

Don't lock the device mutex when wgpu::Buffer::Unmap() or Destory() is
called. This primarily relies on access to buffers being externally
synchronized by the dawn client.

Buffer unmapping shouldn't overlap with other use of the buffer but if
it does a validation error will be thrown. Buffer destroy is similar but
once BufferBase::DestroyImpl() runs there is no option to abort
destroying the buffer. In this case the buffer will spin loop until the
concurrent operation is done and then continue with the destroy.

To guard against concurrent use a new BufferState is added to denote the
buffer is inside an operation. At the start of MapAsync() and Unmap()
the buffer state is updating with compare_exchange, any concurrent
changes will cause compare_exchange() to fail so it can be handled.

The backend may still need to lock the device mutex during UnmapImpl()
if it's not thread safe. For Vulkan and Metal that isn't required so
unmapping a buffer won't block.

Bug: 425472913
Change-Id: I79f8314e8bcbf8a1eb5672cf28e72edb984e7643
